n: Luxury Goods and Real-Asset Hiding by Designated Persons
ds: Designated persons may convert financial assets into yachts, aircraft, art, jewellery, property or collectibles held through intermediaries to avoid freezing. Detection is relevant to banks, art and luxury dealers, brokers, registries and corporate service providers.

cn.rt: Designated persons buying property via home loans or large transfers; branch and digital funding of purchases; art and yachts out of scope.

rat: Yachts, aircraft, art and property held via intermediaries and shell companies; dealers and brokers involved.

ind.n: Purchase of high-value assets by newly formed entities with opaque owners
ind.cx: Yacht, aircraft, art or property is bought through a company with unclear beneficial owners. Real estate held by shell companies with nominee directors.
ind.fp: Privacy-driven structures are common among wealthy buyers. Privacy legislation applies.
ind.ds: Property, art, vessels or other valuables are acquired or held via a company, trust or storage arrangement with concealed beneficial owners.
ind.cn: High-value asset held through opaque vehicle

ind.n: Asset transfers shortly before or after designation
ind.cx: Titles move to relatives, trusts or associates around designation dates.
ind.ds: Titles move to relatives, trusts or associates around designation dates.

ind.n: Maintenance, crew or insurance costs paid by third parties
ind.cx: Running costs of an asset are paid by persons unconnected to the registered owner.
ind.fp: Managers pay on behalf of owners.
ind.ds: Payments are made by parties with no apparent link to the underlying transaction, goods or services.
ind.cn: Payments from or for third parties unrelated to the underlying trade

ind.n: Art or collectibles purchased with no evidence of buyer interest and stored in free ports
ind.cx: Works are acquired and stored without display or documented purpose.
ind.ds: Artworks are acquired and stored long term in free ports with no movement, display or documented purpose.
ind.cn: Art or collectibles held in free ports without display or trade

ind.n: Cash or quick settlement of purchases with source of funds unclear
ind.cx: Large purchase settled via irregular channels.
ind.ds: High-value assets are bought with cash, crypto, third-party or otherwise non-standard funding.
ind.cn: High-value purchases paid in cash, crypto or non-standard funds

ind.n: Vessel or aircraft registered under flags of convenience with managers in secrecy locations
ind.cx: Registration choices obscure the true owner.
ind.ds: Registration choices obscure the true owner.

ind.n: Advisers or agents who act for multiple designated-linked clients
ind.cx: Single broker or lawyer appears across several linked purchases.
ind.ds: A single provider, broker, lawyer or agent sets up entities or handles transactions for many related clients with similar structures.
ind.cn: Adviser or agent acting for multiple linked clients

ctl.ds: Cross-checks asset ownership, title history, security registrations and registry changes against official registers, including for changes close to designation or transaction dates. It confirms that the person presenting an asset genuinely owns it.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Performs and refreshes a documented assessment of inherent risk, controls and residual risk across customers, products, channels, geographies and sectors, and links risks to specific controls and gaps. It directs resources and shapes policy.
Sets internal risk guidance, acceptance limits and approval levels for sectors, commodities and fundraising channels exposed to elevated risk. It gives consistent decisions on how far to engage.

Re-screens the customer base, linked parties and counterparties whenever sanctions or other lists change and on trigger events, with prompt list synchronisation. It closes the gap between onboarding checks and later designations.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Applies enhanced checks to operators, counterparties, storage rationale and transactions that involve free-trade zones and free ports, including facility operator controls. It addresses the opacity and reduced oversight these locations can offer.

Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

Prohibits or caps cash for purchases, loans, donations and settlement above a set value, requiring documented non-cash methods and threshold reporting for dealers. It removes a low-traceability payment route.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

ctl.n: Vessel due diligence and tracking analytics
ctl.ds: Verifies vessel identity, ownership, flag history, insurance and class, and analyses tracking data for gaps, loitering, ship-to-ship transfers and spoofing. It addresses sanctions and illicit-trade evasion at sea.

Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.

ctl.n: Gatekeeper and company service provider due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses licensing, CDD standards and client mix of formation agents, lawyers and similar professionals and monitors formation volumes and concentration. It targets professional enablers.
